qualification_economy: Use the shared native runner, existing capture/eligibility readers and paired-outcome summary. Seven pairing controls and six retained-motion controls join the existing 159-control gate. One 14-world two-interval full canary covers the declared batch size before 224 compact discovery worlds; no full duplicate search.
purpose: Paired timing discovery: 24 exposed pose sequences with fresh original timing and three-times-longer phase holds/delays, each on four of 16 bodies. Both fresh comparators run on every body; all 224 worlds share a twelve-second horizon and inverted start. No gains, poses, slew, actuator limits or eligibility thresholds change.
coverage: Sixteen actual compiled body shapes, nominal actuators and fresh inverted starts
Ninety-six body/profile pairs; each original and slower variant shares body, start, horizon, poses, gains, slew and physical limits
Every body receives six original/slow pairs and both fresh comparators in one fourteen-world batch
All 1440 controller intervals and 7200 native substeps per world retained with compact outcome reconstruction
All paired contact, rotation, eligibility and joint-violation outcomes retained; partial-progress leads remain separate from recovery
selection_rationale: Eight exposed profiles per family span three through six phases, both speed caps and both slew settings. The selection preserves wave_05, impulse_05, waypoint_01 and waypoint_13 failures and the strongest nonviolating impulse_11 observation. Original poses and actuator settings remain fixed; this is exposed development data, not untouched evaluation.
discovery_signal_scope: The existing five-degree gain over the fresh timed comparator and zero-joint-violation screen remains unchanged. Original-versus-slow contrasts are descriptive development diagnostics, not superiority, recovery, training or release qualification.
